newsitem.title: TURKEY: Iraqi opposition welcomes U.S. Iraq strikes.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi opposition welcomes U.S. Iraq strikes.

text.p: An Iraqi opposition group welcomed U.S. attacks on targets in Iraq on Tuesday but expressed concern about the possibility of civilian casualties.

"We welcome any action to reverse (Iraqi President) Saddam Hussein's invasion of northern Iraq," a spokesman for the Iraqi National Congress (INC) told Reuters. "But we are concerned about civilian casualties. Saddam often puts military facilities in residential areas."
The spokesman said he hoped that the military action would be followed by concrete steps, "like extending the no-fly zone or imposing a no armour and heavy weapons zone in northern Iraq."
On Tuesday the United States said it had launched cruise missile attacks against Iraq in retaliation for Iraqi attacks on the Kurdish north.
Iraqi forces attacked the northern Iraqi town of Arbil at the weekend, ousting the Kurdish faction in place there and replacing it with a group more favourable to Baghdad.
U.N. officials said Iraqi forces had withdrawn from Arbil but the United States said this was insignificant as tanks were still outside the town.
